subject: Human Evolution
title: Aquatic Resources
description: Learn Aquatic Resources in one minute.

hook.text: Pinnacle Point Cave on South Africa's coast has 160,000-year-old shellfish remains. Seafood fed early sapiens.

buildup.text: Coastlines offer dense, predictable calories: shellfish, fish, seaweed, and marine mammals.

discovery.text: Omega-3 fatty acids in seafood are critical for brain development—an evolutionary bonus of coastal living.

twist.text: Coastal routes may explain how sapiens spread rapidly: following shorelines provided food every step.

climax.text: The ocean wasn't just a barrier to cross—it was a buffet that fueled migration and brain growth.

punchline.text: The sea fed our brains and our journey.

quiz.question: How did aquatic resources benefit early Homo sapiens?
options: Omega-3s supported brain growth and coastlines aided migration
